atoms.name: Scheduling times and criteria
atoms.one_line: Turnaround = completion - arrival; waiting = turnaround - burst; response = first CPU time - arrival; preemptive schedulers can take the CPU away.

atoms.name: FCFS and Gantt charts
atoms.one_line: Run in arrival order, never preempt; one long job early delays everyone (convoy effect).

atoms.name: SJF and SRTF
atoms.one_line: Shortest burst first (non-preemptive) or shortest remaining time first (preemptive); both minimise average waiting time and can starve long jobs.

atoms.name: Round robin
atoms.one_line: FIFO queue with a quantum; a preempted process joins the queue behind processes that arrived meanwhile; no starvation, more context switches.

atoms.name: Priority scheduling
atoms.one_line: Highest priority runs (lower number usually means higher); preemptive or not; low priority can starve, aging fixes it.

atoms.name: Starvation and fairness
atoms.one_line: SJF, SRTF and priority can starve; FCFS and round robin cannot; aging raises the priority of waiting processes.

atoms.name: CPU utilisation with I/O
atoms.one_line: A process using CPU for c and I/O for i keeps the CPU busy c/(c+i) of the time; n overlapped processes give min(1, n c/(c+i)).

atoms.name: Disk scheduling
atoms.one_line: FCFS, SSTF, SCAN (to the disk end), LOOK and C-LOOK differ in head movement; add distances between consecutive stops, including reversals and jumps.

atoms.name: Real-time: rate monotonic
atoms.one_line: Rate monotonic gives higher priority to the shorter period; preemptive fixed priority; trace releases to find completion times.

patterns.name: SRTF or SJF waiting or turnaround time
